find: \paragraph{ETFs as a wrapper that changes the underlying.}
replace:
\paragraph{Financialization of a non-equity asset class.} The closest structural analogue to our setting is not an equity index inclusion but the financialization of commodities in the mid-2000s, when a new family of index products made an asset class accessible to a clientele that had not previously held it and observed co-movement with equities rose. Tang and Xiong (2012) compare indexed against off-index commodities, which is the design ancestor of our listed-versus-never-listed comparison; Basak and Pavlova (2016) supply the formal counterpart of our equation~\eqref{eq:framework}, in which benchmarked institutional demand raises constituents' volatility and their correlation with the equity market with no change in fundamentals; and Henderson, Pearson and Wang (2015) isolate mechanically driven hedging flow to identify the financial-investor channel, which is the inverse of the basis-versus-allocation decomposition we specify in Section~\ref{sec:framework} and cannot estimate. The strand also contains the standing objection to our own hypothesis, and we would rather confront it than arrive at it independently. Cheng and Xiong (2014) argue that the index-flow explanation for rising commodity--equity co-movement is overstated, and that much of the observed increase reflects shocks common to the macro environment rather than the arrival of the new clientele. That is, in a different asset class, the conclusion our control group delivers. We therefore read our result as an out-of-sample test of their position in a setting where the fundamentals channel they could not shut off, since commodities have real supply and real demand, is unavailable by construction.

\paragraph{ETFs as a wrapper that changes the underlying.}

Substantively, Bitcoin's volatility relative to the equity market fell after the listing while its correlation with equities did not move, and this has to be reconciled with equation~\eqref{eq:framework}, which is written about $\beta$ rather than about $\rho$. On $\beta$ the estimate is not flat: it is
% src: robustness_results.json#outcome_beta.coefficients.d_etf_listed.estimate
$-0.1890$. Our reason for making $\rho$ the headline outcome is an estimation argument and not an economic one. The Fisher-$z$ of a correlation has a sampling variance that depends only on the number of sessions, whereas the sampling variance of a monthly $\hat\beta$ scales with $\sigma_i/\sigma_{mkt}$, which would make the residual variance of the difference-in-differences a function of treatment status. That justifies the choice of estimator; it does not entitle us to describe a decline in the framework's own object as no change. The honest reading is that the loading fell while the co-movement margin did not, and our framework has something to say about that composite. H2's noise-reduction sub-channel, set out in Section~\ref{sec:framework} and then left aside, predicts exactly it: a deep, institutionally arbitraged product displaces the marginal retail investor who reached speculative equities and crypto through the same brokerage application and the same sentiment cycle, which lowers both the sentiment-driven component of co-movement and idiosyncratic volatility. A flat $\rho$, a negative change in $\ln(\sigma_i/\sigma_{mkt})$ and a negative change in $\beta$ is the pattern that sub-channel predicts and that no other hypothesis in our framework predicts. We are not claiming it. With nine placebo donors the smallest attainable randomization $p$-value is $0.10$, $0.20$ is the second-smallest, and $0.20$ will not support a claim. We record it because a reader is entitled to see that the framework speaks to its own results rather than being abandoned at the point where it becomes testable.

The test is short — plot the pre-to-post change in $\ln(\sigma_i/\sigma_{mkt})$ against the change in relative size across the ten coins and ask whether Bitcoin sits on the fitted line — and it is not in this draft. Separately, a randomization $p$-value of $0.20$ on nine donors means that exactly one control coin produced a larger estimate in absolute value, and the identity of that coin is informative in a way its rank is not: if it is DOGE, whose 2021 idiosyncratic episode we flag in Section~\ref{sec:data} as inflating its pre-period idiosyncratic variance, then Bitcoin's rank is being set by a comparison we have already told the reader is contaminated. The nine donor estimates belong in Table~\ref{tab:decomposition} and are not yet there. What the decomposition does establish firmly is that there is no version of these results in which co-movement rose and the correlation measure failed to see it.

find: Two readings are consistent with the evidence. One is that habitat co-movement operates through a shared interpretation of shared cash-flow news — the channel through which ETFs are known to raise systematic price informativeness in equities \citep{glosten2020etf} — and that an asset with no earnings has nothing for that channel to work on. The other is that the effect is present at a magnitude our design cannot resolve. We committed before estimation to distinguishing these by a power criterion, and the criterion returned a verdict between its two bars, so both readings remain open and we decline to choose.
replace: What we are not entitled to say is which channel produced the null, and we state that plainly because the temptation runs the other way. A bounded null on the change in correlation is consistent with at least four structures that our own framework enumerates: that the clientele did not change; that it changed but its discount factor is not equity-linked at the margin; that it changed, transmission occurred, and it was offset by the displacement of a correlated retail noise trader, which is the sub-channel the volatility-ratio result fits; and that the assets which arrived were overwhelmingly market-neutral cash-and-carry positions, so the participation weight barely moved despite the headline figures. Nothing we estimate discriminates among these four. The reading we find most attractive — that habitat co-movement operates through a shared interpretation of shared cash-flow news, the channel through which ETFs are known to raise systematic price informativeness in equities \citep{glosten2020etf}, so that an asset with no earnings has nothing for that channel to work on — is not one of the four, and no number in this paper bears on it. We offer it as a conjecture the result is compatible with, not as an inference from it, and the alternative that the effect is present at a magnitude this design cannot resolve remains open on the power criterion we fixed in advance. Three mechanism margins would begin to separate these structures, all of them estimable on data already assembled for this paper and none of them reported here. A weekend and holiday difference-in-differences asks whether Bitcoin's share of variance and of volume on sessions when US exchanges are closed fell relative to control coins that also trade continuously and also received no listing; it is the one piece of the session logic that survives without intraday history. A liquidity margin is available at no data cost, since Amihud illiquidity and Corwin--Schultz effective spreads require only daily prices and volumes, and a decline in either beside an unchanged correlation would establish that the wrapper changed the asset's microstructure without changing its factor structure, which is the dissociation this section would like to claim and currently cannot. And the summed-lead-and-lag Dimson loading, which we specified and did not report, is the only daily-frequency shadow of the session hypothesis available here. Until those are in the paper, what we have is a bound on the magnitude of the ETF-attributable change and silence on its channel.
source_finding: review#0 (mechanism_reviewer, major concern 1: no mechanism test survives and the conclusion's mechanism claim is unsupported by anything in the paper)
